name: jumplist
description: Read a jump list. automaticDestinations-ms (an OLE compound file): the DestList entries by their version's layout (1, 3 and 4; any other version is refused with a problem and no entries; at most 50,000 entries of one DestList are read, and what follows is named by the stream offset it starts at, as a problem that makes the status partial): entry number, NetBIOS host name, last access (raw FILETIME and ISO 8601 UTC, seven fractional digits), pin state and target path, with the access counters returned raw as undecoded_* and no access count claimed; and every embedded link structure written to out_dir for lnk_parse when write_links is true (an automaticDestinations stream is read whole into memory, up to 32 MiB, because olefile opens a stream whole; a larger one is named and not read, and the status is partial; the file written is mode 0600) (the path, the volume serial and the target timestamps are the link's, not the DestList's). customDestinations-ms has no container: its link structures are CARVED by their 20-byte header, each marked carved, and the container is not parsed. Entries, links and files are paged: `limit` is the bound on the entries shown inline over the whole answer, on the link structures shown inline over the whole answer, and on the files shown inline (not a bound per file, which made it limit squared over a directory), and every row is kept in the file the page names. A FIFO, a socket or a device (named by `path` or found in a directory) is never opened: it is counted under not_attempted and the status is partial. status is complete, partial or failed; the exit status is 1 only when no file could be read. SENSITIVE: the links inside a jump list carry arguments and working directories that can hold a command line with a secret. Writing them (write_links: true with out_dir) is declared secret output: the tool refuses as JSON, before anything is created, unless SECRET_OUTPUT is 1, and out_dir without write_links is refused. The tool has its own clock (114 s of the manifest's 120): when it runs out the read stops, the pages written so far are placed and named, and the answer is partial with a status_basis that says where it stopped and which file and how many files were read; every answer carries status and status_basis (complete only for an input read to its end), a wrong-type argument is refused as JSON (status failed), and SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with one JSON document (status failed with interrupted true, exit 128 plus the signal) and no temporary file. A result file is never replaced: the same result keeps its name, another takes the next free -n name. A file name that is not UTF-8, or a stream name of more than 200 characters, is written under a shortened name and does not stop the run.

path.description: A .automaticDestinations-ms or .customDestinations-ms file, or a directory of them

out_dir.description: Write each embedded link structure here, for lnk_parse to read, with write_links: true: a directory under work/<your id>/ (or work/extracted/<your id>/, work/quarantine/<your id>/; run as a job, a work/<your id>/... path is given $OUT by the harness); anything else in the run, and anything under inputs/, is refused with the places named. Without write_links: true, out_dir is refused

limit.description: Rows shown inline (default 500, 1 to 10000): the bound is on the DestList entries shown inline over the whole answer and, separately, on the link structures shown inline over the whole answer, not on each file (the files page has the same bound); every row is read, every link is written to out_dir, and the whole list is in the file the page names (all_results)

write_links.description: Write the link structures to out_dir (mode 0600). A link keeps its arguments and strings, so this is secret output: refused as JSON, before anything is created, unless the job runs with secret_output (the manifest declares it for this parameter); default false
